verdict.rationale: Blaxel documents sandboxes automatically going to standby (scale-to-zero after 5s of inactivity) and resuming in under 25ms even after weeks. It also documents archiving a sandbox to keep its filesystem and unarchiving it later. The docs do not say that memory or process state is preserved, and the pause is triggered by inactivity rather than by the developer. missing for 10: explicit documentation that memory/process state survives standby, a developer-triggered pause/resume API, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pause a running sandbox and resume it later with filesystem and memory state intact

citations.quote: Automatic scale-to-zero after 5s inactivity, resume from standby under 25ms even after weeks.
Sandboxes resume from standby in under 25 milliseconds and automatically scale to zero after a few seconds of inactivity.
Archive a sandbox to keep its filesystem while shutting it down, and unarchive it later to get it back.
Create point-in-time snapshots of sandboxes, roll them back to a checkpoint, and fork them into new sandboxes.
